claim: Sphinx is a Git hook that asks the developer a question about what agent-written code does before it ships.
quote: Sphinx is a Git hook for agent-assisted development. Before your agent’s code ships, it asks you a question about what that code actually does.

claim: It is free, open source, MIT licensed, installed via npm.
quote: npm install -g sphinx-understand ... sphinx · MIT licensed

claim: On pushes to protected branches Git waits until the user passes; wrong answers get an explanation and a new scenario.
quote: When you push to a protected branch, Git waits while Sphinx asks you to predict what your change will do. If you miss something, it explains and gives you a new scenario to try. Once you pass, the same push continues.

claim: Questions come from a separate reviewer model that does not see the coding conversation.
quote: The questions come from a separate reviewer model. It reads the committed change through read-only Git tools and does not see the conversation that produced the code.

claim: Questions target behavior and failure modes, and the check is open-book.
quote: Questions cover behavior, failure modes, and invariants rather than file names or function names. The check is open-book

claim: Works with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi or plain Git; answers never reach the coding agent.
quote: Works with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and Pi, or plain Git. Your answers never reach the coding agent

claim: Reviewer can run on a Claude Code/Codex plan, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; Sphinx has no hosted service.
quote: Sphinx has no account or hosted service of its own.

claim: A typical check makes about 5-8 model requests and there is no default cap.
quote: There is no default cap on model calls. A typical check makes about 5 to 8 requests, plus about one per answer.

claim: Authors state it is practice, not a security gate, and can be bypassed; the LLM examiner can be wrong.
quote: This is practice, not a security gate. Anyone with local access, including a coding agent, can bypass hooks or get outside help. Passing does not prove who wrote the code or that you understood it unaided. The examiner is an LLM and can be wrong.

claim: Changed code is sent to the reviewer provider; ignore rules won't catch secrets pasted into source.
quote: Code leaves your machine. The reviewer provider receives the changed code and related files from the commit, your answers, and `.sphinxcontext.md`. ... Ignore rules match file paths, so they will not catch a secret pasted into ordinary source.

claim: v0.1 covers only local commits and pushes, not web merges, CI or deployments.
quote: Version 0.1 checks local commits and pushes only. It does not cover web merges, CI-required checks, or deployments.

claim: Small changes get up to one question; large ones up to three at default depth.
quote: small changes get up to one question (none for documentation or trivial edits), and large ones up to three at the default depth.

claim: Skips and yolo toggles are logged; a pass lasts 24 hours.
quote: Every skip and yolo toggle is logged with its reason ... A pass lasts 24 hours, unless the code, destination, or policy changes.

claim: The authors' evaluation used only five small synthetic repos and is not an all-green result.
quote: These are development measurements on five small, synthetic Git repositories, not a certification of arbitrary code reviews. ... The result is **not an all-green semantic evaluation**, despite all 560 guarded unit/integration tests passing.

claim: No tested reviewer model is established as reliably correct; a correct answer was rejected (false negative).
quote: No tested route is established here as reliably correct for arbitrary repositories or answers.

claim: A stronger model (Sonnet 5.5) reproduced the grading false negative.
quote: This reproduced the material false negative.

claim: npm package sphinx-understand latest version 0.1.11, first published 2026-10-16, MIT.
Show HN posted 2026-10-18 got 252 points and 89 comments.
quote: Show HN: Sphinx – A hook that quizzes you on your AI's code before shipping ... 252 points

claim: HN objection: users can just paste the question into their agent.
quote: Nothing prevents a lazy person from copy-pasting the question to the agent so I'm not sure that it would be an effective gatekeeping mechanism.

claim: HN objection: devs would have their agent remove the hook.
quote: they'd probably just ask their agent to remove the hook anyways like they do with our husky hook.

claim: HN objection: understanding what a PR does differs from knowing whether it's wrong.
quote: Maybe the useful distinction is understanding what a PR does versus knowing how to tell if it’s wrong. A quiz can check the first, but the second is often where review matters most.

claim: HN objection: tool won't reach the people who need it.
quote: People who care about the problem will definitely not be using this as a method to "understand" their code. People who don't care about this problem will continue to not care. So, who is this for?

claim: Similar prior tools exist (PEAK, about 6 months earlier, with anti-cheat; vibecheck.dev).
quote: We built something quite similar 6 months ago called PEAK (Proof of Effort And Knowledge).

claim: Supportive HN view: it tests the person instead of adding another AI reviewer.
quote: I like that it tests whether the person understands the change instead of adding another AI reviewer.

claim: The epigraph, which the page credits to 'Sun Tzu', comes from an X post by @yacineMTB (kache), which the page links.
quote:
you can outsource your thinking
but you cannot outsource your understanding

claim: The demo exchange on the landing page is illustrative, not real output.
quote: An illustrative exchange. Real questions come from your diff.
